title: Protocol for in vitro sonoporation validation using non-targeted microbubbles for human studies of ultrasound-mediated gene delivery
protocol: Fix the transducer on the holder of the tube rack, and place in the water tank.
Adjust the height of the stage according to the focal length of the transducer and ensure the focal point covers the sample tube.
Connect the transducer with impedance match that is connected to the Sonic Concepts system using a waterproof BNC-UHF cable.
Fill degassed DI water in the tank and top off the tube stage.
Generate cell pellets of 2 × 10^5 cells in 0.5-mL Eppendorf tubes and suspend in 100 μL degassed PBS (+/+).
Mix with 2 μL of PI, 0.2 μL of Cal Green and 5 μL of activated microbubbles.
Add the mixture to the cell suspensions.
Add degassed PBS (+/+) to achieve a total volume of 125 μL in the sample tube.
Thoroughly mix the solution but avoid splashing the liquid into the tube lid.
Generate cell pellets of 2 × 10^5 cells in 0.5-mL Eppendorf tubes and suspend them in 100 μL degassed PBS (+/+).
Mix 9 μg of plasmid with 5 μL of activated Definity microbubbles, then add to the cell suspensions.
Add degassed PBS (+/+) to achieve a total volume of 125 μL in the sample tube.
Thoroughly mix the solution.
Avoid liquid splashing into the tube lid during mixing.
Transfer the tube containing the cell mixture to the sonoporation apparatus immediately after mixing.
Rotate the tube if there is a delay to keep components mixed and prevent settling.
Enter ultrasound parameters through a computer in 'Remote' mode or input them directly from the front panel in 'Local' mode.
Set the frequency to 250 kHz.
Set the burst length to 33 ms.
Set the period between bursts from 500–4000 ms.
Set the total treatment time to 180 seconds.
Set the peak negative pressure (PNP) from 100–200 kPa, which corresponds to a system setting of 200–900 mW.
Insert the Eppendorf tube into the place holder at the center of the ultrasound focus after thorough mixing of the solution.
Place an acoustic absorber on top of the Eppendorf tube to ensure ultrasound waves do not escape into the surrounding environment.
Press the ‘START’ button on the RF drive amplifier and trigger the ultrasound application on the tube.
Take off the tube from the sonication apparatus.
Rotate the tube for 5 minutes at 20°C.
Fix the tube using rubber bands on a rotator for thorough mixing of the sonoporated cells and plasmids.
Add 375 μL of PBS (+/+) to the sample to achieve a total volume of 0.5 mL.
Take out 10 μL of sample and thoroughly mix with 0.4% (w/v) Trypan Blue solution (10 μL).
Draw 10 μL of mixture and add to the cell counter.
Centrifuge the cells in the tube at 300 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Discard the supernatant.
Prepare the samples for confocal imaging.
Resuspend the cells in 4% PFA using 100 μL.
Incubate for 10 min at 20°C in the dark.
Centrifuge the cells at 300 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Discard the PFA and wash the cells with PBS.
Centrifuge again at 300 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Discard the PBS.
Resuspend the cells in 30 μL of DI water.
Add the cell suspension to a glass slide and spread the cells in a circle within a 12 mm diameter.
Let the cell suspension dry for at least 30 min at 20°C.
Add a drop of antifade mount reagent on the dried cell samples.
Place the coverslip carefully on top for further confocal imaging.
Set up the microscope with appropriate imaging settings.
Select the 40x oil lens objective for microscopy.
Adjust laser intensity and emission filters according to specifications.
Calibrate motorized stage for precise movement.
Use excitation peak of 566 nm and emission peak of 574 nm for PI staining.
Use excitation peak of 506 nm and emission peak of 531 nm for Cal Green staining.
Adjust confocal parameters using control samples stained with only PI or Cal Green, as well as unstained cells.
Image the experimental samples after calibration.
Acquire images with specific imaging parameters such as focal plane, exposure time, and laser intensity.
After sonoporation, add plasmid-treated cell suspension to a well of a 6-well plate containing 875 μL cell growth media.
Put plates into the cell-culture incubator.
Collect supernatant samples from wells after 24-h or 48-h incubation using sterile pipette.
Transfer collected supernatant to sterile tubes for storage at 4°C.
Gently wash cells with PBS (−/−) to remove residual media.
Aspirate the washing solution.
Add 0.5 mL of TrypLE Express to cover the cells.
Incubate at 37°C for 5–10 minutes (usually appropriate for hMSCs).
Check the cells under a microscope to ensure they are in a single-cell suspension.
Gently mix the cells with a pipette.
Transfer detached cells to sterile tubes.
Seed cell samples on uncoated 12-mm coverslips for confocal microscopy analysis of adherent cells, allowing them to adhere during culture.
Do not use TrypLE Express to harvest cells from coverslips.
Centrifuge the cell samples in a TrypLE-treated cell tube (300 × g, 5 min, 4°C) and discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the cells in 150 μL of PBS (−/−).
Add the samples to the wells of a U-bottom 96-well plate.
Centrifuge the plate (300 × g, 5 min, 4°C).
Invert, flick and dab the plate to ensure all liquid is removed.
Resuspend the cells in 100 μL Live/Dead Blue mix (1:500 dilution in sterile PBS (−/−)).
Incubate for 20 min at 4°C in the dark.
Add 100 μL of PBS (−/−) and centrifuge the plate (300 × g, 5 min, 4°C).
Invert, flick and dab the plate to remove PBS (−/−).
Resuspend the cells in 200 μL of PBS (−/−).
Prepare compensation controls using a well with unstained cells.
Add a well with Live/Dead stained cells.
Include a well with a drop of GFP compensation beads in 175 μL of PBS (−/−).
Examine the samples using a Guava EasyCyte Flow Cytometer.
Process the data with FlowJo Software for analysis.
Create a gate for single cells based on forward scatter (FSC) and side scatter (SSC).
Set a live/dead discrimination gate based on Live/dead blue stain to exclude dead cells.
Identify the GFP+ cell population relative to negative control samples.
Wash the cells in 6-well culture plates with 1 mL PBS.
Repeat the aspiration/wash step twice.
Fix the cells with 500 μL of 4% PFA for 10 min at 20°C in the dark.
Aspirate the PFA and repeat the aspiration/wash step.
Stain the cell nuclei with 500 μL DAPI working solution for 10 min at 20°C in the dark.
Mount the coverslip with the cell samples onto a glass slide using a drop of antifade mount reagent.
Set up the microscope with appropriate imaging settings.
Use a 20x dry lens or 40x oil lens for microscopy.
Adjust laser intensity and emission filters according to requirements.
Position the motorized stage for precise sample movement.
Capture multiple images of adjacent regions ensuring complete specimen coverage.
Acquire each image with consistent focal plane, exposure time, and laser intensity.
Use DAPI: Ex = 355 nm, Em = 461 nm; mNG: Ex = 506 nm, Em = 517 nm settings.
Prepare a working solution of Capture Antibody using PBS (−/−).
Add 100 μL of Capture Antibody to each well in the 96-well plate.
Seal the plate and incubate for at least 12 hours at 20°C.
Discard solutions and wash wells twice with Wash Buffer.
Incubate plates with Reagent Diluent (300 μL) at 20°C for at least 1 hour.
Add 100 μL of the sample per well.
Add 100 μL of standard samples to other wells.
Seal and incubate plate for 2 hours at 20°C.
Repeat washing step after incubation.
Add Detection Antibody to each well according to the manufacturer’s protocol.
Streptavidin-HRP is added to each well according to the manufacturer’s protocol.
Substrate Solution is added to each well according to the manufacturer’s protocol.
Stop solution is added to each well according to the manufacturer’s protocol.
Repeat Step when changing the solution.
Immediately measure the optical density of each well at 450 nm with a microplate reader.
Use a reference wavelength of 570 nm to correct for any background signal.
Record the readings and use them to calculate the concentration of the analyte in the sample.
